+ +  M O R E   M A I L ! ! + +

   March, 1991      Page  Reply

   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

           From: Ettrick Thomson
Dear Brian,
I'm puzzled by your reply(OUTLET
42, More Mail,P.10) to my letter
(P.8) about "FOR A=A TO...".Your
SAM doesn't seem to work the
same as mine. Enclosed is a
program, essentially the same as
that in my letter but it also
prints the address "a" of the
first of each group of 8 bytes.
As expected, the address "a"
keeps on increasing to cover the
24 bytes starting at 12345...

10 FOR a=12345 TO 0: NEXT a
20 FOR i=1 TO 3: PRINT a;":";
30 LET s=0: FOR a=a TO a+7
40 PRINT PEEK a;",";
50 LET s=s+PEEK a
60 NEXT a: PRINT s: NEXT i

Brian Cavers to Ettrick Thomson

You're absolutely right. I think
I completely misunderstood you
in the first place. I did a test
and found that FOR a=a to a+7
failed on SAM and jumped to the
conclusion it always failed and
so assumed your solution was
wrong. I now see that it only
fails if "a" has previously been
declared as a normal numeric
variable rather than a FOR-NEXT
variable. If it has been already
declared as an earlier FOR-NEXT
variable then it's OK.Your loop:
FOR a=12345 TO 0 which, on the
face of it, seems to do nothing,
is actually initializing "a" as
a FOR-NEXT variable. Thanks for
persisting with me Ettrick.
                        - Brian

From I.A.G. Ross, RENFREWSHIRE



Dear Ron and Brian,



             BETADOS
             -------

During the review of BETADOS by
Brian Gaff in OUTLET 41 it was
pointed out that Dave Hood's
program, ORGANISER, locks up if
an attempt is made to use it
with BETADOS. I wrote to Dave
Hood about this and he was kind
enough to give a remedy...

1.Go into BASIC (Select RENAME)
  then multiple; select any prog
  and input Z(capital) x(lower
  case).

2.LIST and ENTER. Delete lines
  16 & 17.

3.Type 6390 RETURN and ENTER

4.Type GO TO 7500 and ENTER

5.Save ORGANISER via MAINTENANCE



Observations:

1.The Sector check will not work
if disc booted with BETADOS. It
will work if booted with GDOS.

2.Copying files (from disc 1 to
disc 2): Computer does not NEW
itself if operating with BETADOS
and snapshots can be copied.

3.The rearrangement of programs
will not work happily with discs
containing more than 80 files.
Extra ones will be eliminated.

4.The altered version of ORGAN-
ISER will also work with PICK-
POKEIT and PLUS D HACKER and
will operate the sector check.

        Yours sincerely,

           I.A.G. Ross

Thank you for the info.
                         - Brian

From Keith Pirie, ABERDEEN


Dear Ron and Brian,

I hope that a "my word processor
is better than your word
processor"argument is[sic] about
to be started. I always think
that if a program, no matter
what kind,suits the needs of the
user, then its use should not be
criticised. So, Tasword, Word
Master,the Last Word, The Writer
et al,all have different ways of
treating text;all have different
additional features and so on
but let's not get drawn into
arguments. Everyone to his/her
own - that's called freedom of
choice!!

Can I thank Malcolm Perry for
solving my problems with Tasword
/Fastword changeability.


Anyway, onto other things. Like
a lot of you other readers I
bought a SAM in the early days
but returned it due to a list of
complaints the length of your
arm. I have now re-invested and
am delighted that my confidence
in the Miles Gordon partnership
has been renewed. I do find it
difficult to give up my Spectrum
and seem to have had little time
so far in working with the SAM
as I know I should. It tends to
be "better the devil you know"
when it comes to using software.

I have one or two queries that
perhaps others have met and have
cured. All help will be grate-
fully accepted:-

1. I seem to get a lot of track
problems on disks. I have not
experienced this with my Plus D
and the disks I am using on the
SAM are from the same supplier.
They are formatted on the SAM.
Is there a problem with the SAM
internal disk drive?

2. When I save art work from
"FLASH" to disk and reload it as
a SCREEN$ file it invariably
flashes. How can this be cured?

3. I cannot get OVER to work in
MODE 3. The manual says it works
but it just doesn't.

4. Likewise the SCREEN and OPEN
SCREEN commands I am having
problems with. How do you write
information to the SCREEN in
background mode?

Perhaps the root of my problem
lies in knowing what these comm-
ands do on the Spectrum and ex-
pecting them to the same on SAM.

Here's a little tip in exchange
for solving my problems (he said
hopefully!) When encountering
track problems I have run disks
through"The Organiser" by Better
Bytes and repaired the offending
sectors, unlocking the files
behind the corrupt area. It lets
me transfer the files to another
newly-formatted disk.
                  - Keith Pirie

Brian Cavers to Keith Pirie


Thanks Keith.

Yes, there is a serious problem
with the hardware. If you press
RESET while a disc is in the
drive it is likely to corrupt
the disc. Always remove any disc
from the drive before pressing
RESET.An alternative is to enter
RUN USR 0 which resets without
affecting the drive. It is not
known if this problem affects
all SAMs but it is wise to play
safe even though it is an
infernal nuisance and I still,
occasionly forget and ruin a
disc. ALWAYS keep a separate
back-up disc of important discs.

The only other likely cause of
your problem is if you are still
using an early DOS. Don't use
anthing before DOS 2.0. I doubt
that you are but just in case.

We have had problems with three
of our five SAM drives but this
has mainly been an intermittent
"hang-up" where a drive will not
respond or even just sits with
the motor going round and round.
I have not been able to pin down
the cause for this.

I abandoned OVER in Mode 3 or 4
long ago. It seems to me that it
would have been quite legitimate
for MGT to simply say it's a
Mode 1 command only and most
people would have accepted that.

You mean to PLOT, DRAW, PRINT on
an "invisible" screen? Try...

 10 SCREEN 1: MODE 4: CLS #
 20 PRINT "SCREEN 1"
 30 CLOSE SCREEN 4   (see below)
 40 OPEN SCREEN 4,4
 50 SCREEN 4
 60 PALETTE 7,99
 70 DISPLAY 1
 80 PRINT "SCREEN 4" (invisible)
 90 PAUSE: DISPLAY 4: PAUSE
100 SCREEN 1

CLOSE before OPEN to avoid error
if already OPEN (see line 30).
PLOT,DRAW, PRINT etc. act on the
"current" screen while another
screen is DISPLAYed.PALETTE acts
on the DISPLAYed screen NOT the
current screen (bug?).Try moving
line 60 past 70.

I always recommended ANTIFLASH
(OUTLET 37)to stop FLASH screens
flashing but now Adam Inglis has
a better solution (see the next
letter).

                        - Brian

From: Adam Inglis

Try resetting the colour before
SAVEing a SCREEN$ in 'FLASH'
[select "COLOUR O.K." from the
SCREEN options sub-menu]. This
stops the flashing colours prob-
lem - very simple if you think
about it!
           Adam Inglis

Many thanks, Adam - an extremely
useful tip! That "COLOUR O.K."
doesn't even seem to be in the
manual and didn't appear to do
anything so I guess most of us
just ignored it! Your solution
will save me and other users the
aggravation of having to keep
reloading screens into programs
like ANTIFLASH!          - Brian

From Bill Clarke


Have you anything suitable for
video titling in the pipeline?

Could you include motor coaches
in the clip art?

Re: video signal from +3. I have
wrote three times; enclosed SAE
for reply. No luck apart from
one reply in OUTLET stating you
know the details but are loath
to give same.

          Bill Clarke


Brian Cavers to Bill Clarke.

Sorry, Bill. I searched my stock
of clip art but can't see any
for motor coaches. Can anyone
else help? If Keith Pirie is
reading this, Keith, you've sent
us some great clip art. Have you
got anything or can you produce
anything on motor coaches?

Re: video titling, we have the
excellent QUANTEL in this issue
for switching screens and you
can create various text styles
using a mixture of JUMBOCHARS
(OUTLET 19 - order the tape copy
as it's not available on +3);
DUBTEX(OUTLET 31); CLIP COMPOSER
(OUTLET 29); RTCLIP (OUTLET 30)
and RTCLIPAID (OUTLET 36).

Both JUMBOCHARS and DUBTEXT need
a tiny amount of BASIC programm-
ing ability whereas RTCLIPAID is
as easy as typing but is limited
to one text size. If you can do
a little BASIC you can mix and
match ordinary text, DUBTEX,etc.
You can also enhance the text by
mixing it with some of the clip
art we feature every month using
CLIP COMPOSER.

Re:the +3 video signal, we can't
run a free service by private
correspondence.Some replies need
hours of work which can only be
justified if shared with others.
Queries are answered in these
pages. If you write to a solici-
tor for legal advice he'll send
a bill whereas a legal column in
a magazine is free!

I've not looked up my reply but
I seem to remember I simply said
I thought it inappropriate to
give you a technical reply -
especially since I'd not tried
it myself on a +3 but only on a
standard Spectrum. I also seem
to remember hearing since then
that my idea doesn't work on a
+3 so it's just as well! I think
your later letter was in these
pages but again, I don't think
we had the full answer. Please
believe me, there is no intent
to withold information! We are
always willing to help readers
but we don't know everything and
often have to rely on our other
readers for information(which is
another good reason to publish
letters!).

Having said all that - and to
prove how wonderful our readers
are - we've now received exactly
the help you need in detail from
Simon Greenfield in the follow-
ing letter. Please let us know
how you get on.

                        - Brian

From: Mr. Simon Greenfield.

I would like to point out that
KWIKCAL doesn't work as it gives
you wrong dates. If you compare
any month with that of a printed
calendar,e.g.,according to KWIK-
CAL Xmas this year falls on a
Sunday; my birthday in September
falls on the wrong day making me
5 days older than I am. Although
the program was written for 1991
it also gives wrong dates for
previous years.

I'm probably going to get some
flack for saying that 'BIRDMAN'
was pathetic - no, I couldn't do
any better, but it was much like
seeing the early days of the
Spectrum with its matchstick man

type programs, yet this was on
the SAM version of OUTLET. Is it
possible to keep these sort of
programs for the Spectrum and
use something that makes better
use of the SAM's graphics and
sound for the SAM version of the
mag? Sorry to sound so mean.

The new 'MASTERDOS' is truly a
must, well worth the fifteen
quid with its extra features.
e.g. DIR$, DSTAT, FSTAT, FPAGES,
BACKUP commands and the ability
now to format a disk to hold
either 80, 98, 198, 778 files on
a disk (the latter only giving
you some 605K per disk) these
being for your subdirectories if
you so choose to create. Then
there's PATH$, DATE$, TIME$ the
other features are endless.

This DOS appears somewhat
similar to my father's ADFS DOS
(ADVANCED DISK FILING SYSTEM)
for his Acorn Electron, though
much more powerful- a real must.
I strongly urge users with disk
drives to buy this new DOS. It
even lets you create 5 RAM disks
to any memory size (depending on
your SAM's available RAM)though,
if you have the 1 MEGA-BYTE
memory packs fitted, you are
also blessed with an extra 40
Dos variables to play with.

Did you manage to suss out the
bug in the prog. for formatting
DS/DD disks to 800K for the +3's
external B drive? A M/Code list-
ing appeared in the CONTACT mag.
(13)from Garner Designs for the
very same program and may help.

Here's how to go about fitting
and obtaining a composite video
signal from a Spectrum +3...


You first need a phono plug
socket - obtainable from Tandys.


Solder some wire to the correct
positions of this plug then take
your +3 apart (gently).


Looking at the PCB, look for the
DIODE marked D31 about an inch
down from the bottom right hand
corner of the RF modulator (big
shiny metal box top left corner)
and just in front of an 18-leg
chip marked IC9.

Solder the centre wire of your
phono plug to the LEFT LEG of
the DIODE D31.Care must be taken
not to overheat this diode. Try
putting a small blob of solder
on the diode's leg before
offering up the wire and melting
the two together with a brief
touch of the soldering iron.

Bend up the middle tag on the
left of the lid of the RF modul-
ator (smallest one) then solder
the outer braid to that tag. You
may need help doing this. Bring
the new socket out of the +3 via
the TV opening or simply melt a
small trough in the edge of the
casing then assemble and Bob's
your uncle - one composite video
socket for quick VCR recordings
off your computer's signal!

I must stress this mod was done
on my 1988 Spectrum +3 and works
ace but may not be quite the
same for later models.

An RGB adapter can be had for
the earlier 128K+, and grey +2
Spectrums from an advert out of
the back pages of Camcorder User
and Video Camera mags from -


       HALL VIDEO PRODUCTS
      147 GLADSTONE STREET
            WINSFORD
            CHESHIRE
             CW7 4AU

         TEL:0606 551925
    (8:30a.m to 7p.m Mon-Sat)

They also sell Video titling
packages for the Spectrum range.
Prices are as follows -

     SUPERINTRO          `15
     PROTITLER           `25
     48K CV SOCKET        `4
     128K+/128K+2 ADAPTER `5
     (not for latest +2A)

     SPECIAL OFFER BOTH
     PROGRAMS + SOCKET
     OR ADAPTOR          `35

          P&P included

State make/model when ordering.

I myself use PROTITLER +3 and
highly recommend it.
             - Simon Greenfield

Brian Cavers to Simon Greenfield

Thanks for that info, Simon.

Regarding your criticism of the
BIRDMAN program, it should be
remembered that the central pur-
pose of OUTLET is to be just
that - an outlet for users to
share their programs, ideas and
info.BIRDMAN is unsophisticated,
simple programming but what it
does it does well and utilizes a
useful principle that can be ex-
amined in the listing.

I regret that I do receive some
programs that are ten times more
clever than BIRDMAN but don't
work properly and are so badly
programmed I am unable to make
them work!

We often forget that many users
have only had their computer a
short time and are in the same
position that you and I were in
1982 to 1983. Nothing's changed.
In 1983 you could have bought a
much more sophisticated machine
and laughed your hat off at the
things that fascinated us on the
Spectrum.

When assessing contributions I
have to decide what readers will
enjoy - no matter how trivial. I
am often surprised to find that
a program I thought rather weak
brings in letters of delight! I
have lost count of those who've
written saying how much they
enjoyed the little bird flying
out of the tree in Issue 24's
title page!

I'd like to add that items like
BIRDMAN should not be taken too
seriously. They are a tiny part
of the magazine - like cartoons
in a newspaper -You just glance
over them, smile - and read on.

Still,your views are welcome and
I promise not to have a stickman
stickbird, stick train, stick
traffic and stick BEEPs together
in any single program in OUTLET
again this year. Promise.

I'm still trying to contact the
author of the 800K FORMAT.I know
of the listing but assume it's
the same listing which does not
work. You might disassemble our
code and check it line for line
with the +3 User Group listing..

From D.E. Ottery, SOMERSET

I wish to congratulate you on a
well-put-together magazine that
caters for those of us who do
more than just play games.

My SAM is fitted with one inter-
nal drive and also connected via
the external drive interface to
the 3.5" drive from my Plus D
package for use as a second
drive. My Citizen MSP20 printer
is likewise shared between both
computers. To avoid unnecessary
damage to the ends of drive and
printer cables when swapping
between machines, is there any
way I can obtain a "Data Switch"
box (as advertised fo use with
PCs to share printers) to allow

me to use both drive and printer
plugged into a box and manually
switch control from Spectrum to
SAM?

Are you going to be at the next
All-Formats Show (March 23rd)? I
saw you there at Christmas but
was unable to make it to the
February show.


I really know very little about
BASIC and nothing about machine
code but I want to learn.Can you
run "A Thicky's Guide To Machine
Code" sometime in the future. I
know OUTCLASS does this but I
can't follow much of it!

              - D.E. Ottery

Brian Cavers to D.E. Ottery

There was an excellent article
by Malcolm Perry on sharing a
drive using a printer switch in
DRIVECHAT in OUTLET 40.

Yes, we plan to be at the next
All-Formats Fair if possible. I
hope we'll see you there.

The first OUTCLASSes were aimed
at the beginner. They all appear
on the compilation Spectrum disc
OUTLE EXTRA 1. When I compiled
that disc I re-read all the text
to see if it needed re-writing
but although I'm fanatically
meticulous in refining text over
and over I couldn't find one
thing I wished to change.

Of course, EXTRA 1 is not avail-
able on SAM but it is possible
to read the articles. If you
order the Disciple version of
EXTRA 1, the OUTCLASS files can
be displayed thus: Load any SAM
OUTLET. Press ESC and enter...

300 LOAD"outclas04"+CHR$175 CODE


RUN the program and select any
text item such as EDITORIAL and
it should load the first of the
OUTCLASS articles. Others have
the same name but numbered 05,
06 and 10 to 13. You can see the
names by doing a DIR but CHR$
175 will appear as NEW.The first
of the two OUTCLASSES on machine
code is "outclas12"+CHR$ 175.

I must remind you that OUTCLASS
was written for the Spectrum. If
you are serious about learning
machine code you must really buy
an assembler (see reviews in
OUTLET 37)to type in the program
listings. You should also buy
the SAM technical manual from
SAMCO to study the simple ROM
calls that will enable you to do
much for very little, e.g. just
printing text on screen is not
easy for beginners but call a
ROM routine and you don't even
need to know how it works.

You never learn much by merely
reading. Type in the listings in
SAMCLASS each month,save and run
the code -then try modifying it.
                        - Brian

From Peter Wright, W. YORKS.

You recommended a +D. Who from?
What sort of drive? Am I correct
in assuming you use a Disciple?
I assume the +D will fit into
Interface 1 so I can copy from
microdrive to disc?

I presume all previous problems
with SAM loading Spectrum prog-
rams are now solved. Do you mean
to give it the once over and
report its suitability?

As I use many amateur radio pro-
grams and find that all are now
for either the Beeb or the IBM
I'm in somewhat of a quandary
whether to get a +D and drive, a
SAM or an IBM compatible.

I'm surprised you praise the
opposition: "LET'S COMPUTE"; you
might lose some members to it.

               - Peter Wright

Brian Cavers to Peter Wright.

DATEL, Govan Road,Fenton Indust-
rial Estate, Fenton, Stoke-on-
Trent, ST4 2RS sell the +D with
a standard 80-track drive for
`129.99 inc. postage. Telephone:
0782 744707.

However, the +D CANNOT be used
in tandem "piggyback" with the
Interface 1 because there is no
through port on the +D and no
"isolation" button. Still, you
can move files across by saving
first to tape then reloading.

The Disciple CAN be connected at
the same time as Interface 1 and
you can switch between them so
you can load from microdrive and
save to disc.

I'm not sure if you can still
get Disciples from Rockfort
Products. They were at 81 Church
Road, London NW4 4DP but ring
them first on 01 203 0191. The
last advert I have for them is
nearly two years old and the
Disciple with one drive was on
sale for `130.00. Amazingly,that
is the same as the +D now!

You would probably be better
advised to order from MICROSNIPS
at 37 Seaview Road, Wallasey,
Merseyside, L45 4QN (Tel: 051
630 3013) although their price
is a staggering `179.95 + `10
delivery for a Disciple with one
drive. You can get SAM with one
drive for under `200 so that has
to be considered.

Loading Spectrum programs into
SAM is still a grey area. There
are many conflicting reports. It
depends enormously on what cass-
ette recorder you use. I bought
a Sony TCM-818 from Curry's in
the early days as recommended by
MGT. I have found it needs to be
up full volume and any tape with
a weak signal will not load. My
main hifi deck is far better.
However, I have heard others say
the Sony is fine! I regret that
I can't guarantee you'll be able
to transfer programs via tape
without problems but you might
get lucky and have no trouble at
all!(except for some games with
special loaders). Once I had got
the level right I could always
transfer programs (now I do it
direct via Disciple disc).

I can't advise you on the PC but
if you know lots of the programs
you want are available on an IBM
and you can afford to pay the
much higher price then go for it
(remember OUTLET is not on PC!).

As for us, both Ron and I have a
Disciple system and twin drives
each as our main systems. Ron
also has a +D for testing, extra
duplicating capacity,back-up and
development.

Regarding telling readers about
"the opposition", we firstly are
trying to provide a service and
only SECONDLY a profit. Thus we
report whatever is available so
you can choose. That's why we're
so poor of course but loved by
one and all.            - Brian

From Brian Thompson,WARWICKSHIRE

Dear Ron and Brian,

I bought a SAMSUNG 14" portable
TV with a SCART connection(Model
CI-3312Z), from my local dealer
(Langhams of Rugby and Daventry)
at a cost of `179.99 compared
with `229.99 for the Sony.

I connect SAM, with a scart lead
which I had previously obtained
from MGT, switch on, but nothing
happens. I check everything but
still no picture.

Back to the shop, which I reach
about 1pm. The dealer is puzzled
but I explain that I know SAM
works OK with a SONY. The dealer
promises to come out later.

At 4.30pm the dealer arrives and
says he has phoned SAMSUNG (UK)
and the problem's known to them.
A diode (D502 I believe, but
please check)must be replaced by
a germanium diode or bypassed.
He gets out his soldering iron
and the result is happiness all
round.

I hope this is helpful, the
details can easily be confirmed
by a phone call to SAMSUNG.

Issue 42 has just dropped thro'
the door and I am pleased to see
that we now have SAMCLASS. How-
ever I see we have lost OUTCLASS
for which I am sorry. I suppose
it is too much to ask to have
both? [sound of sobbing - BC].

Incidentally I have just tried
to print out SAMCLASS but it
stops at page 20 with the error
messsage "4 Subscript wrong,
1705:4. I use an Amstrad DMP2000
printer with a 512k Sam through
an external drive interface.

               - Brian Thompson


I will consider adding OUTCLASS
to ADD-ENDERS.

The printing problem has now
been solved. You should be able
to load the article into this
issue and print it. Alternative-
ly, the cure is to change the
A$(P TO) in line 1705 and 1708
to A$(P TO LEN A$-1).
                        - Brian.

PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE! Text is accepted in any form for OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files (say which),typed or handwritten letters. Please state if there should be parts of your letter you do not wish published but we always use our discretion anyway. Letters may also be edited for clarity and length... Please ask if you welcome direct correspondence from other OUTLET readers and we will publish your full address.

From: Ettrick Thomson Dear Brian, I'm puzzled by your reply(OUTLET 42, More Mail,P.10) to my letter (P.8) about "FOR A=A TO...".Your SAM doesn't seem to work the same as mine. Enclosed is a program, essentially the same as that in my letter but it also prints the address "a" of the first of each group of 8 bytes. As expected, the address "a" keeps on increasing to cover the 24 bytes starting at 12345...

10 FOR a=12345 TO 0: NEXT a 20 FOR i=1 TO 3: PRINT a;":"; 30 LET s=0: FOR a=a TO a+7 40 PRINT PEEK a;","; 50 LET s=s+PEEK a 60 NEXT a: PRINT s: NEXT i

Brian Cavers to Ettrick Thomson

You're absolutely right. I think I completely misunderstood you in the first place.
